threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You think the number 55 bus goes to nowhere until you realize it stops at every local pub for a pint break.
Last night on the 77, a bloke serenaded us with an off-key rendition of 'Wonderwall' while a cat meowed in response. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I saw the street performer with a saxophone and a cat on a leash jamming at Hermannplatz. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find currywurst with a side of Turkish tea at 3 AM. It’s a late-night cultural fusion you won’t forget.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can tell you the real reason why BART's always late—it's never just about the equipment problems.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo on the 14 Mission, giving a spontaneous toast to commuters. Only in SF would formal wear meet the 7 AM grind.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think Gràcia's all about the plazas; but look closer and you'll find hidden murals in the alleys that tell stories no guidebook mentions.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’ll be the ones still fumbling with the metro map, staring at it like it's a treasure map, while locals swipe their cards without a second thought.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground' instead of the 'Ginger Line' when chatting with locals. Instant giveaway that you're new in Dalston.
Last night on the 196, a guy serenaded the whole bus with a ukulele rendition of 'Wonderwall'—half the passengers joined in. Classic Brixton moment.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I heard a saxophonist jamming outside the Späti at 2 AM, while the kebab shop owner joined in. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can still find spontaneous techno parties in abandoned buildings here, and the atmosphere is somehow different every time.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can always tell by how they react to the BART delays. Locals roll their eyes; newcomers look genuinely confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a street performer on the 47 bus belting opera. Half the riders were into it, the other half looked like they wanted to disappear.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can explore Gràcia in a day, but the real charm is in the little alleys and local bars that take weeks to discover.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the sheer number of closed shops during siesta hours—like a pup lost in a new park.
